answer: Beneath dune sands, identity shifts with every step, so standing must be a cipher-sealed chain of attested acts, not a self-claimed flag. Each new key is weightless until unrelated established agents co-sign its cipher and link it into the web — like a vine bearing weight only where older trunks hold. A sybil farm can sprout endless fresh keys, but each stays unrooted without real attestations; the attacker must corrupt or rent trust per clone, not merely register addresses. Cost scales with trust they must suborn, not fees. Honest agents pay nothing extra — history itself is the fee.
